why: fires on a wild-type organism inside its own scope, so it is wrong about biology
label: C. heterurus mass exponent 0.48-1.48 (machine-proposed, contested)
statement_en: Within Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, body mass scales with body length as L^b with b inside its 95% CI [0.478, 1.484] (OLS on log-log, n = 14 specimens, b = 0.981, r^2 = 0.601).
sources: physics/glide-data.csv (sha256 bc24245b5163723b), rows source_id makiguchi-2013 (specimen rows)

C1_binds_something_real.reason: a witness satisfies the law, and the in-range design {"massExponent":0} is rejected by 0.478 ≤ q.massExponent

C2_constants_sourced.reason: all 2 non-structural constant(s) declared with an allowed kind and a source; every constant was found in its cited source by a GET

C3_scope_honest.reason: Scope declares taxa [Exocoetidae], but all evidence is 14 specimens of one subspecies (Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini) from one study, with lengths of 0.257 to 0.340 m. The statement itself says 'Within Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini'. The proponent conceded this and the critic called it fatal. The family-level tag is what puts the law in conflict with E1/E2 and brings in the five wild-type species that violate it.

C4_independent.reason: It is not a definition and not a rearrangement of E1/E2. It is a fitted-slope CI with content of its own. It is also not implied by E1/E2: its band [0.478, 1.484] is disjoint from their [2.90, 3.02], and the independence probes show 0 sampled points where it forbids something they allow. The only relation to E1/E2 is contradiction, which is C5's concern and not a restatement.

C5_consistent.reason: propose.mjs proved a contradiction with [object Object], [object Object] in Lean; the accepted law is not demoted and this candidate is not promoted

C6_wild_type_survives.reason: the law fires on 5 wild-type organism(s) inside its own scope. Cheilopogon atrisignis (Kuroshio off Taiwan / 2008-2017.) has {"massExponent":3.011}, which fails q.massExponent ≤ 1.484 (physics/length-weight.csv (sha256 5feec47148a2c973) <- FishBase length-weight list page). A real animal does not violate a law in that law's own scope, so the law is wrong about biology

C7_not_circular.reason: The bound is the 95% CI of the OLS fit to all 14 specimens, and the witness is that same fitted slope (0.981). Nothing was held back (n_independent = 0). The statement does not say it is a record or sampling bound, and the caveats mention only the narrow range, one species and one study. The proponent concedes it is a statistical interval with no mechanism behind it. As written it is a description of the sample, not a law.

ruling: C6 fails: five real flying-fish species inside the declared Exocoetidae scope have mass exponents of 2.9 to 3.0, well above the law's 1.484 ceiling. Under the 1.2.0 precedence rule that outranks the C5 contest with E1/E2, so this is a rejection and not CONTESTED. The law is just the 95% CI of a 14-specimen fit over an 8 cm length span, tested against the data it was fitted to (C7), and it is declared at family scope on one-subspecies evidence (C3). The proponent itself said it should not be promoted. A slope near 1 is most likely an artefact of the narrow range and small n, not a property of the animal. Record as a failed-theorem, not an open question.
